title.narrative: Towards improving water security by Aquifer Storage and Recovery for banana production in the Magdalena Delta, Colombia

description.narrative: The project followed the planned activities, with some adjustments along the way.• Evaluation of Application Conditions (A1) began with processing collected data to assess the feasibility of Aquifer Storage and Recovery (ASR). The relative risk and expected ASR performance were initially meant to be evaluated for six sites. However, since Banasan was a project partner while Tecbaco was not, the focus shifted to assessing the three Banasan sites, and the Tecbaco sites were discarded. Based on the reviewed conditions, the most suitable site was selected for further assessment, and the necessary data for site-specific hydrogeologic characterization was identified.• Site Characterization (A2) involved collecting subsurface data, groundwater level information, and water quality samples. Initially, the plan was to subcontract Hidrogeocol, a trusted partner in Colombia, but internal changes in the company prevented their collaboration. This led to delays in securing a suitable subcontractor and executing the field activities.• ASR Pilot Conceptual Design (A3) proceeded as planned, with the development of a conceptual ASR system tailored to the selected site.• Stakeholder Engagement and Water Governance (A4) was closely coordinated with the Water Stewardship Platform for the Río Frío and other watersheds. This collaboration ensured strong local participation in the project's two planned workshops. The first, held in month 2, introduced the project to stakeholders, while the second, in month 12, presented findings and outlined next steps. These workshops saw broad representation from governmental entities (Parques Nacionales, Corpamag), agricultural businesses and guilds (banana and palm oil sectors), NGOs (WWF, Fundación Banasan), and community and indigenous organisations.• Project Coordination and Communication (A5) were carried out as planned. In addition, the Banasan communications team provided extra support, contributing to the production of a project video that helped disseminate the project's objectives and results.The project has successfully achieved several key results:1. Identification of a Suitable ASR Site: A site with significant Aquifer Storage and Recovery (ASR) potential was identified at the farm of the beneficiary. Despite suboptimal hydrogeology, other favorable conditions such as existing infrastructure, seasonal freshwater needs, and lack of alternatives deem the site viable for ASR implementation.2. Conceptual ASR System Design: A comprehensive conceptual design for the ASR system was established to guide decision-making and investment processes for a pilot project in the region. Various design options were assessed, including the regeneration of an existing well versus constructing a new one. The impact of an ASR system on the farm's water balance was calculated, along with the improvement in irrigation water quality. Due to certain uncertainties, a range of potential outcomes was provided, along with necessary pre-treatment measures for infiltrating surface water. This detailed information facilitated the beneficiary's decision to invest in the pilot project with their business partners.3. Ground Truthing and Stakeholder Engagement: Collaborative efforts with local partners and the beneficiary ensured active participation in technical discussions, fostering trust and a clearer perspective on future decisions. Partial and final results were communicated to local stakeholders, enhancing transparency and engagement.4. Stakeholder Education and Nexus Analysis: Initial steps to engage stakeholders involved educating them on ASR techniques and their environmental and agricultural impacts, facilitated by the Water Stewardship Platform. A subsequent workshop presented the potential regional impact of upscaling ASR on water availability, sparking interest among stakeholders to explore further partnerships. The innovation of introducing ASR technology in a coastal area, new to Colombia, highlights the indispensable knowledge brought by the consortium, which has been highly appreciated by stakeholders.
